question: The ordered pair $(1,-2)$ satisfies the system $(k+1)x+2y=3$ and $3x-y=5$. Determine $k$, and write the resulting system in matrix form.
explanation:
Verification of the second equation
For $x=1$ and $y=-2$, $$3x-y=3(1)-(-2)=5$$ Hence, the ordered pair satisfies the second equation.
Substitution in the parameter equation
Using the first equation, $$(k+1)(1)+2(-2)=3$$ Therefore, $$k+1-4=3$$
Determination of the parameter
Simplifying gives $$k=6$$
Resulting matrix equation
The system becomes $7x+2y=3$ and $3x-y=5$. Its matrix form is $$\begin{bmatrix}7&2\\3&-1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}3\\5\end{bmatrix}$$
